prose.label: Amazon S3 and Azure Blob Storage.
Amazon Security Lake.

checks.do: Whether the S3 bucket's default encryption is Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3), since selecting AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS) makes the connection fail.
Whether alert rules are still associated with an integration before deleting it: an integration associated with alert rules cannot be deleted until they are moved to another integration.
Whether the Security Lake custom source uses the Security_Finding event class.

tool-types.statement: ZPC can be integrated with SIEM and ITSM tools, cloud storage services (such as Amazon S3) and ChatOps tools like Slack.

quotes: SIEM and ITSM tools for data analysis, incident management, and remediation.
Cloud storage services such as Amazon simple storage service (Amazon S3) and send the system audit logs and alert notifications to an S3 bucket for further evaluation.
ChatOps tools like Slack and send notifications to specific Slack channels.

cloud-storage-list.statement: ZPC can be integrated with Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage and Amazon Security Lake, and the integration lets ZPC send alert data logs to them.

quotes: The integration enables ZPC to send the alert data logs to these cloud storage services.
- Amazon S3
- Azure Blob Storage
- Amazon Security Lake

admin-only.statement: Only ZPC administrators can configure cloud storage integrations.

quotes: Only ZPC administrators can configure cloud storage integrations.

status-values.statement: On the Integrations page the cloud storage integrations list shows Status (Success, Failed, Paused or Pending, the outcome of the previous data transfer) and Data Transfer (Enabled or Disabled).

quotes: Status: The outcome (Success, Failed, Paused, or Pending) of the previous data transfer.
Data Transfer: The state (Enabled or Disabled) of data transfer.
evidence.after: Last Sent: The date and time when the data was last sent to the storage service.

data-transfer-default.statement: For the cloud storage integrations on the Integrations page, data transfer is enabled by default and can be disabled with a toggle to pause without deleting the integration; a transfer already in progress completes before it is disabled.

quotes: By default, the data transfer is enabled.
If any data transfer is in progress, the activity is completed and then the data transfer is disabled.
If you want to pause the transfer without deleting the integration, select the toggle to disable the data transfer.
evidence.after: Last Sent: The date and time when the data was last sent to the storage service.

log-type.statement: The Log Type of cloud storage and ITSM integrations is Alert or Audit Logs, and the ITSM list shows IT Service (Jira or ServiceNow) and Hostname.

quotes: Log Type: The type of data log (Alert or Audit Logs) that is sent to the storage service.
IT Service: The name of the service (Jira or ServiceNow).
Hostname: The host name for the service.
Log Type: The type of data log (Alert or Audit Logs) that is sent to the IT service.

slack-channels-column.statement: The Slack integrations list shows Channels as the number of channels added for sending notifications.

quotes: Channels: The number of channels that are added for sending notifications.

s3-setup.statement: For Amazon S3, the S3 bucket policy copied from ZPC must be applied to the bucket, the Folder Location is optional, and Test Connection verifies the connection.

quotes: The policy authorizes ZPC to access the S3 bucket.
9. (Optional) For Folder Location, enter the folder location of the bucket.
11. Click Test Connection to verify the connection between ZPC and Amazon S3 service.
7. Click the Copy icon to copy the S3 Bucket policy.
On the Edit bucket policy page, paste the S3 bucket policy and click Save changes.

s3-encryption.statement: For the Amazon S3 integration the bucket's default encryption must be Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3); selecting AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS) makes the connection fail.

quotes: Select Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) as the encryption key type for the connection to be successful and eventually for seamless data transfer.
If you select AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS), then the connection fails.

s3-pending-status.statement: A new Amazon S3 integration shows Pending because no data has been sent; alert rules must be configured and associated with the integration for ZPC to send data logs, after which the status changes to Success.

quotes: The initial status is shown as Pending because data is not yet sent to the Amazon S3 bucket.
You must configure and associate the alert rules with this integration for ZPC to be able to send the data logs.
After ZPC sends the data logs to the Amazon S3 bucket, then the status changes to Success.

blob-setup.statement: For Azure Blob Storage, ZPC uses a storage account connection string, and a Container Location folder name is optional but the folder must first be created in Blob Storage.

quotes: A connection string includes the authorization information required for ZPC to access data in your Azure Storage account.
8. (Optional) Enter a folder name for the Container Location. It is mandatory to first create a folder in your Azure Blob Storage and then add the name.

blob-pending-status.statement: A new Azure Blob Storage integration shows Pending until alert rules are associated and ZPC sends data logs, after which the status changes to Success.

quotes: The initial status is shown as Pending because data is not yet sent to the Azure Blob Storage.
Once ZPC sends the data logs to the Blob Storage, then the status changes to Success.
You must configure and associate the alert rules with this integration for ZPC to be able to send the data logs.

splunk-cim.statement: ZPC data logs conform to the Splunk Common Information Model (CIM), and S3 or Azure Blob Storage can be integrated with Splunk using the Splunk Add-on for AWS or Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services.

quotes: Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC) has designed the data logs to conform with the Splunk Common Information Model (CIM).
- Splunk Add-on for AWS
- Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services

edit-cloud-storage.statement: Editing an Amazon S3 integration requires testing the connection again, and changing the Amazon S3 Bucket Name or Folder Location requires testing again; for Amazon Security Lake the page lists the Integration Name, IAM Role, Amazon S3 Bucket Name, Folder Location and Bucket Region as editable, and does not itself say a retest is needed.

quotes: Whenever you edit an Amazon S3 Bucket integration, you must test the connection again.
If you change the Amazon S3 Bucket Name or Folder Location, you must test the connection again.
For Amazon Security Lake, change the Integration Name, IAM Role, Amazon S3 Bucket Name, Folder Location, and Bucket Region as required.

delete-cloud-storage.statement: A cloud storage integration associated with alert rules cannot be deleted until the alert rules are moved to another integration; the Delete button stays disabled.

quotes: You cannot delete an integration if it is associated with alert rules. You must first move the alert rules to another integration. Until then, the Delete button is disabled.

asl-overview.statement: Zscaler is regarded as a source integration for Amazon Security Lake, which uses OCSF for the alert information and requires the Parquet file format for stored alerts.

quotes: Amazon Security Lake uses the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) as the selected format for the alert information and requires the Parquet file format for the stored alerts.
Zscaler is regarded as a source integration for Amazon Security Lake.

asl-custom-source.statement: The Security Lake custom source must use the Security_Finding event class, is created in the region where the AWS console is connected (which must be specified in the ZPC Security Lake integration), and its data source name determines the S3 path for alert files.

quotes: Event class: Make sure you use the Security_Finding event class.
The custom source is created in the region where the AWS console is connected.
This name determines the path in the S3 bucket to which the alert files will be written.
You need to specify this region while setting up the Security Lake integration on the ZPC Admin Portal.

asl-ids.statement: The custom source takes the ZPC AWS Account ID and External ID copied from the Cloud Storage page in the ZPC Admin Portal, and the ARN IAM role from the custom source is entered in ZPC as the IAM Role.

quotes: Account ID: Enter the account ID that you copied from the Cloud Storage page in the ZPC Admin Portal.
External ID: Enter the external ID that you copied from the Cloud Storage page in the ZPC Admin Portal.
This role allows the ZPC AWS account to write data to Security Lake.
Copy the ARN IAM role. You need to provide this value while setting up the Security Lake integration on the ZPC Admin Portal.
IAM Role: Enter the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) ARN role that you copied after creating the custom source.

asl-test-connection.statement: For Amazon Security Lake, Test Connection validates that the S3 bucket exists.

quotes: The test connection validates that the S3 bucket exists.

asl-partitioning.statement: Alerts are written to Security Lake as Parquet files; a new file is posted when the file size reaches 256 MB or after 5 minutes, under the folder structure region=<awsregion>/accountid=<cloudaccountid>/eventDay=<YYYYMMDD>.

quotes: A new file is generated and posted whenever the file size reaches 256 MB or after 5 minutes.
The folder structure is: region=<awsregion>/accountid=<cloudaccountid>/eventDay=<YYYYMMDD>.
ZPC alerts are exported in Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) format to Amazon Security Lake and are stored in Parquet files.

asl-alert-rule.statement: A Security Lake alert rule is created with Alert Type Cloud, and its scope can be filtered by Business Units, Clouds, Accounts, Regions or Tags and its policies by Compliance, Severity, Threat Category and Policy Type.

quotes: - For Alert Type, select Cloud.
You can filter the scope by Business Units, Clouds, Accounts, Regions, or Tags.
You can filter the policies by Compliance, Severity, Threat Category, and Policy Type.

asl-ocsf-static.statement: The OCSF static values are category_name Findings, category_uid 2, class_name Security Finding, class_uid 2001, metadata.product.name zpc, metadata.product.vendor_name zscaler and metadata.version 2.2.

quotes: | category_uid |  | 2 |
| class_uid |  | 2001 |
| metadata.product.name |  | zpc |
| metadata.product.vendor_name |  | zscaler |
| metadata.version |  | 2.2 |
| category_name |  | Findings |
| class_name |  | Security Finding |

asl-ocsf-cloud-map.statement: In the cloud alert payload, OCSF severity maps from the risk field, finding.uid from alert_id, finding.title from policy_name and time from csp_event_timestamp.

quotes: | time | csp_event_timestamp |  |
| severity | risk |  |
| finding.uid | alert_id |  |
| finding.title | policy_name |  |

asl-ocsf-iac-map.statement: In the IaC alert payload, OCSF time maps from alert_created_dt, severity from severity, and cloud.provider from scan_plugin.

quotes: | time | alert_created_dt |  |
| severity | severity |  |
| cloud.provider | scan_plugin |  |

asl-ocsf-status.statement: OCSF activity and status map from the alert_status field and status_detail from alert_status_description.

quotes: | activity | alert_status |  |
| status | alert_status |  |
| status_detail | alert_status_description |  |

asl-troubleshoot-glue.statement: If ZPC alert data is in the Security Lake S3 bucket but the Glue Crawler fails to parse it, the page says this typically occurs when the custom source uses the wrong event class and must use the Security Finding event class.

quotes: This issue typically occurs when the custom source that is created for the integration is using the wrong event class. Make sure you create the custom source with the Security Finding event class.

asl-troubleshoot-failed.statement: A Failed status on the Security Lake integration indicates ZPC does not have permission to access the Amazon Security Lake S3 bucket.

quotes: This indicates that ZPC does not have the permission to access the Amazon Security Lake S3 bucket.

asl-troubleshoot-not-exported.statement: If new alerts are in the ZPC Admin Portal but not exported to Security Lake, the page says to check the alert rule notification configuration and the alert rule scope.

quotes: Make sure you've configured the alert rule notification and check the scope of the alert rule.

servicenow.statement: ZPC leverages ServiceNow APIs to create incidents when a security policy violation occurs; setup needs the ServiceNow hostname, username and password, and the instance must be online.

quotes: You can integrate ZPC with ServiceNow to create incidents on ServiceNow whenever a security policy violation occurs on the selected cloud accounts.
Ensure that your ServiceNow instance is online.
- For ServiceNow Hostname, enter the ServiceNow hostname.
- For ServiceNow Password, enter the password for ServiceNow.
ZPC leverages ServiceNow APIs to automatically create tickets when a misconfiguration is detected.
- For ServiceNow Username, enter the username for ServiceNow.

jira-oauth.statement: The Jira integration works with Jira cloud versions that support the required authentication mechanism and APIs to create a Jira task, and requires an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app configured in the Atlassian Developer console first.

quotes: ZPC can be integrated with Jira cloud versions, provided there is support for the required authentication mechanism and APIs to create a Jira task.
You must first complete the OAuth configuration before integrating ZPC with Jira.
2. Click Create and select OAuth 2.0 integration.
1. Log in to the Atlassian Developer console.
3. Under Create a New OAuth 2.0 (3LO) integration, enter a name for the application.

jira-scopes-callback.statement: For the Jira OAuth app, example scopes are read:jira-work (read project and issue data) and write:jira-work (create and edit issues), the Callback URL is the application URL copied from the ZPC Admin Portal, and the Client ID and Client Secret are entered in ZPC.

quotes: For example, select read:jira-work to read the Jira project, issue data, etc. Select write:jira-work to create and edit issues in Jira.
13. For Callback URL, paste the application URL you copied from the ZPC Admin Portal.
16. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret.
- Jira Client ID: Paste the Client ID that you copied while configuring the OAuth app.
- Jira Client Secret: Paste the Client Secret that you copied while configuring the OAuth app.

jira-authorize-failure.statement: If Jira login is not possible after clicking Authorize, ZPC shows an Authorization in Process message, and the page says to check and use the correct Jira Client ID and Client Secret.

quotes: Click Authorize to validate the Jira connection.
If you're not able to log in, then you see the Authorization in Process message in the ZPC Admin Portal
Check and use the correct Jira Client ID and Client Secret values for the authorization to be successful.

itsm-edit.statement: Editing an ITSM integration allows changing the ServiceName and using Reset Validation to validate the ServiceNow hostname and credentials.

quotes: 1. Change the ServiceName.
2. Click Reset Validation to validate the ServiceNow hostname and credentials if required.

delete-itsm.statement: An ITSM integration associated with alert rules cannot be deleted until the alert rules are moved to another integration.

quotes: You cannot delete an integration if it is associated with alert rules. You need to move the alert rules to another integration, then you can delete this integration.

slack-limits.statement: The Slack integration needs an Incoming Webhook (only one webhook per Slack channel), and ZPC allows 10 channels per integration, with another integration needed for more.

quotes: - You can add only one Webhook per Slack channel.
- ZPC allows you to add 10 channels per integration. You can configure another integration to add more channels.

slack-edit.statement: When editing a Slack integration the Integration Name can be changed and more channels added, but existing channel and webhook details cannot be edited.

quotes: Change the Integration Name.
Click Continue Editing if you want to add more channels.
You cannot edit the existing channel or Webhook details.

delete-slack.statement: A Slack integration associated with alert rules cannot be deleted until the alert rules are moved to another integration.

quotes: You cannot delete an integration if it is associated with alert rules. You must first move the alert rules to another integration.

asl-ocsf-blanks.title: Why some Amazon Security Lake OCSF mapping rows are blank or NA
asl-ocsf-blanks.detail: The OCSF tables leave rows blank or NA (attacks.0.tactics.0.uid, attacks.0.technique.uid) without explanation; only a subset of mapping rows is claimed here.

asl-policy.title: The S3 access policy for Amazon Security Lake
asl-policy.detail: The Security Lake page tells readers to apply 'the required policy' for S3 access without giving it.

integrations-list-asl.title: Whether Amazon Security Lake appears in the Integrations page list
integrations-list-asl.detail: The About Third-Party Integrations page names Amazon S3 Bucket and Azure Blob Storage as the Cloud Storage service, while the Adding Cloud Storage Integrations page also lists Amazon Security Lake. The claims state what each page says.

integration-limits.title: Limits and roles for integrations
integration-limits.detail: The number of integrations per tenant, the ServiceNow roles required and Jira permissions beyond the example scopes are not stated in the captured pages.
